questions.prompt: What generic-reasoning floor must a result meet?
questions.description: The completed ObservedBool result ends at one primitive true/false conflict and is excluded under every option.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Require injectivity or disequality to derive an equality or disequality over equality-sort children, then require a distinct real EggCC consumer to use that intermediate fact. Fixed-input knockout and mediation-rescue controls must show that the intermediate fact causes the endpoint.

questions.prompt: When should a hand-written equivalent disqualify the result?
questions.description: Every finite inference can be expanded into several custom rules, so this decides whether the objection is specifically the one-simple-rule shortcut or any manual equivalent.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Disqualify a result when one constructor-specific primitive comparator can reproduce the endpoint from the same seeds. Allow a larger faithful manual implementation as the required fair comparator, without claiming unique logical power.

questions.prompt: What finite search portfolio should end in failure if no qualifying payoff appears?
questions.description: Each family gets one eligibility screen, one smallest actual-host/native probe if eligible, and at most one revision for a concrete falsifier. A family closes immediately on its declared early falsifier.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Search the scoped fixed-shift chain, the same-mask Bitand reverse-disequality chain, and then screen fixed-split tuple cancellation as a reserve. If all three close without a pre-existing baseline bug or repeated end-to-end speedup, mark the goal failed; do not add another family silently.
